subject: PPU mapping & private-offer token economics — follow-up
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Kwon <daniel.kwon@acmeai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-22T10:12:00-08:00
Subject: Quick follow-up: token volumes & target $/1M for marketplace private offer

Hey Daniel — great chat this morning. Thanks for walking through Acme AI's planned workloads. Quick recap and next steps so we have alignment before I loop in Marketplace ops:  

Summary from call:
- Current production: ~700M tokens/month for generation workloads (inference + prompt tokens).
- 12–18 month growth target: 3–6x depending on feature rollouts (conservative planning: 2.5x in Q1-Q2).
- You mentioned procurement prefers AWS private offer route to centralize billing.

What we need from you to map PPU (price-per-1M tokens) scenarios into a Marketplace private offer:  
1) Target unit price goal (your target $ per 1M tokens) or budget range for the first 6–12 months.
2) Any committed-minimum token bands procurement would consider (monthly or annual).
3) Confirmation that AWS private offer is the desired procurement flow (yes/no).

Attachment: pp_map_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet) — I put three example pricing bands and mapping notes for AWS private offers. If you can reply with the three items above, I’ll draft the private-offer playbook and loop in our marketplace lead + your procurement contact.

Proposed next steps:
- You confirm (1)-(3) above — ideally by EOD Friday.
- I’ll share a draft Private Offer (PO) language and three PPU scenarios for review.
- If approved, we coordinate with AWS Marketplace to issue the private offer and then finalize purchase order.

Thanks — Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0198

Attachment: pp_map_v1.xlsx (3 sheets)

From: Daniel Kwon <daniel.kwon@acmeai.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@acmeai.com>
Date: 2026-11-22T12:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up: token volumes & target $/1M for marketplace private offer

Ben — thanks for the clear recap and for the XLS. Quick answers below:  

1) Target unit price: we'd like to aim for ~$950 / 1M tokens as a target for the first 6 months. If we can get to $700 / 1M with a meaningful commitment it would be ideal.
2) Commitment bands: Procurement is comfortable discussing a 6–12 month committed band. Rough bands we could sign up for: 1) 1M tokens/month (pilot), 2) 3M tokens/month (scale), 3) 6M+ tokens/month (enterprise).
3) Procurement flow: yes — AWS private offer is preferred so cost hits our central billing and we can adhere to internal invoicing controls.

Budget note: We’ve scoped a Q1 spend target of $8k–12k/month but that assumes pilot-level throughput and optimized prompt engineering. If we hit 3M/month quickly the budget flexes upward to $25k–40k/mo.

I attached a short procurement checklist we use (acme_po_requirements.pdf) to make sure the offer matches our PO template. Happy to hop on a 20-minute follow-up with your marketplace lead if that helps.

Thanks,
Daniel
Daniel Kwon
Head of Platform | Acme AI
daniel.kwon@acmeai.com | +1 617-555-0124

Attachment: acme_po_requirements.pdf

Daniel — perfect, this is exactly what we need. I sketched three concrete PPU scenarios that map to AWS private-offer constructs; see summary below and attached draft PO language. I’ll open a HubSpot deal update after this note.

High-level PPU scenarios (maps to private offer tiers):
- Pilot | Band A: $1,200 / 1M tokens — commitment: 1M tokens/month (1–3 month pilot). Minimal commitment, higher unit price.
- Scale | Band B: $950 / 1M tokens — commitment: 3M tokens/month (6 months preferred). Your "target" price sits here.
- Enterprise | Band C: $700 / 1M tokens — commitment: 6M+ tokens/month + 12 month term. Best unit economics if Acme wants predictability.

Unit economics notes:
- We modeled the blended effective $/1M over a 6-month ramp (attached pp_map_v1.xlsx shows examples).
- For AWS private offers the marketplace flow requires a private-offer ID and an agreed unit in AWS terms; our marketplace ops team will translate these PPU bands to AWS usage units (we'll share the exact unit-conversion table).
- If Acme wants to cap monthly spend we can include spend caps in the private-offer contract and map to purchase order lines.

Next steps I propose:
1) Ben to share private-offer draft (attached) and HubSpot link for signature.
2) Acme procurement to confirm desired band (A/B/C) and preferred commitment term.
3) Karthik to coordinate with AWS Marketplace to generate the private-offer ID and confirm unit mapping to AWS usage reporting.

Attachment: private-offer-draft.docx (contains proposed PO language + spend cap examples)

If that looks good I’ll kick off the Marketplace coordination and set up a 20-min ops sync with Karthik + your procurement lead.

Thanks — Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
